title: Penne al Salmone
subtitle: Smoked salmon and cream pasta
excerpt: Penne in a light cream sauce with smoked salmon, dill, and a little lemon. The salmon goes in off the heat so it warms through without cooking to a tough, dry texture.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pasta with smoked salmon and cream became a popular Italian-American and European home dish in the 1980s. In Italian trattorias it is found along the northern Adriatic coast and in the north of Italy, adapted to the availability of smoked salmon. The version here keeps the cream sauce light so the salmon remains the focus.

content.text: Penne al salmone is a light cream sauce that works precisely because the salmon does not cook. The sauce is made, the pasta is cooked, and the smoked salmon goes in when the pan is off the heat. It warms through gently and stays silky rather than turning grainy. Dill is the right herb here; parsley works but dill and salmon have a specific affinity.
Cook the penne in well-salted boiling water. Reserve a cup of pasta water before draining.

While the pasta cooks, melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the shallots and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the white wine and simmer until reduced by half, about 3 minutes.
Add the double cream and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until slightly thickened. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.

Remove from the heat. Add the drained penne and toss to coat, adding a splash of pasta water if the sauce is too thick. Add the smoked salmon strips and dill. Toss gently, the residual heat will warm the salmon through. Serve immediately.
